sections.content:
7,270 people

were counted on the census as "information technology trainers" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Information technology trainers provide instruction in the use of computers for professional and personal purposes and advise on, plan and organise IT training within industrial, commercial and other establishments.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "information technology trainers", 14% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "information technology trainers" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.footer: Source: Census 2021 from Office for National Statistics

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "information technology trainers" included:

  • other drivers and transport operatives
  • registered mental health nurses
  • managers and directors in retail and wholesale

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "information technology trainers" there were a similar number of men and women (45.1% compared with 54.9%).

This means "information technology trainers" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "business and public service associate professionals".

Men made up 45.1% and women made up 54.9% of "information technology trainers"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "information technology trainers" included:

  • data entry administrators
  • solicitors and lawyers
  • fitness and wellbeing instructors

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "information technology trainers" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "information technology trainers" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "information technology trainers", 11.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (77.1% compared with 22.9%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (89.3%) than self-employed (10.7%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was London. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Birmingham, this is in the region of the West Midlands.
